prerequisites: It is recommended to have prior knowledge of the English language, starting from an A1 level to reach an A2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
To enroll in this course, it is necessary to pass or be enrolled in all courses from previous years to the one in which this course is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Oral and written communication of knowledge in a foreign language.
Foster the development of the English language in the field of engineering and its practical application of grammatical, lexical, and cultural knowledge.
Develop linguistic awareness of English as a second language, its grammatical and lexical mechanisms, and forms of expression.
Develop listening and reading comprehension skills, as well as oral and written expression skills in technical English.
Develop grammatical and lexical notions of the English language and understand the basic structures of technical English.
Stimulate student autonomy and critical capacity for understanding texts, dialogues, and oral presentations.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Skills - Writing, reading, and presenting facts and numbers correctly in a professional setting.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Understanding symbols and abbreviations.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Presenting data: Interpreting and describing graphs, charts, and diagrams.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Language - Expressing numbers and calculations.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Expressing measurement and technical specifications.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Saying temperatures.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Saying dates, websites and email addresses.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Language for talking about trends.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Adjectives and adverbs.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Prepositions.
UNIT 1: NUMBERS AND TRENDS - Describing timelines.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Skills - Describing uses, appearance, and definitions.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Giving a short presentation: Structuring a presentation, exploring effective presentation strategies.

UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Language - Language of description (e.g., It's really + adj./ It can + verb/ It looks like, it is shaped like /It is in the shape of ...); defining relative clauses, reduced relative clauses.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Adjectives and qualities, order of adjectives.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Comparing and contrasting; superlative adjectives.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Nouns and adjectives connected with geometry and properties.
UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Reason and purpose - Conditionals.

UNIT 2: DESIGN AND INNOVATION: DESCRIBING PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGIES - Language for presenting: Key words and phrases for introducing, and concluding your presentation, signposting language for linking ideas; language for dealing with questions; persuasive language.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Skills - Describing a process; explaining a process using a diagram; discussing the stages of production.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Writing clear instructions and warnings.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Language - The Passive Voice: present simple passive structures.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Verbs for manufacturing operations.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Imperatives for instructions and warnings.
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Language for sequencing instructions and processes (sequence words).
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Adverbials of time (once, while, before and after).
UNIT 3: GIVING INSTRUCTIONS AND DESCRIBING A MANUFACTURING PROCESS - Prepositions.
4. INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL: REPORT WRITING - Skills - Writing a short report: general guidelines (structure, format, and style).
4. INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL: REPORT WRITING - Writing a short report about a problem.
4. INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL: REPORT WRITING - Language - Possibility and Probability.
4. INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL: REPORT WRITING - Past simple and Present Perfect.
4. INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL: REPORT WRITING - Time expressions.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Skills - Identifying your personal strengths, key skills and experience.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Writing a short CV.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Talking about your CV.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Writing a cover letter.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Preparing a job interview: asking and answering interview questions.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Learning strategies to build applicant's confidence.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Language - Phrases for demonstrating personal strengths and weaknesses.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Phrases to give details of your personal characteristics, qualifications, transferable skills, professional experience, etc.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Action verbs; positive adjectives, positive expressions.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Softening negative information and highlighting positive information.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Avoiding spelling mistakes.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Revision of past form of verbs, and prepositions.
5. JOB SEARCH: PREPARING FOR A JOB INTERVIEW - Useful language for opening, main body and closing cover letters.
teaching_methods: Lectures (Explanation of linguistic content and its application for learning theoretical contents)
Autonomous problem solving (Exercises related to linguistic skills and communicative skills, especially speaking)
ICT-supported practices (Practice of the four communicative skills: listening, speaking, reading, writing, and linguistic skills of Technical English, individually and in groups)
Tutored work (Analysis and resolution of practical exercises related to grammatical and lexical content and communicative skills, both in and outside the classroom, especially writing)

assessment_methods.method: Practical exercises / Application of linguistic content (Use of English)

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation systems: continuous and global. For continuous evaluation, the final grade is 100% based on coursework and tests; a minimum average of 5 points is required, with a minimum of 4 (out of 10) in each part (Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing, Use of English). If any part is below 4, the final average will be capped at 4.5. Students scoring below 4 in any skill must retake only those parts in the July exam; failure in July requires retaking the entire course in subsequent academic years. For global evaluation, a single final global test applies the same weighting scheme and minimum passing conditions; students failing the first opportunity must retake the entire course in subsequent calls. Plagiarism in any work or activity will result in an automatic failing grade (0.0).
